subject: french

moments.title: L'Etranger
moments.body: Camus's novel of an Algerian-born French clerk who kills an Arab on a beach defines the literature of the absurd.
moments.takeaway: Camus's work emerged from his Algerian roots.

moments.title: La Peste
moments.body: Camus's plague novel becomes an allegory for occupation and resistance.
moments.takeaway: Fiction can hold political and metaphysical questions together.

moments.title: Camus dies in car crash
moments.body: Camus dies aged 46 with an unused train ticket in his pocket.
moments.takeaway: Some biographies become inseparable from the work.

now.title: Camus today
now.body: La Peste returned to bestseller lists in 2020 during COVID. Postcolonial readings (Kamel Daoud's Meursault, contre-enquete, 2013) continue.
now.open_questions: How do we read Camus alongside Algerian voices?

reflection: A pied-noir who never quite settled in either France or Algeria gave the language a new register.
